tool.name: NoiseAtReceivers

param.name: sources
param.displayname: Sound sources (point layer with h_src and Lw_63 ... Lw_8000)
param.dialogReference:
The point layer with the noise sources. One point = one source.
Needed fields: h_src (height of the source above ground, m) and Lw_63, Lw_125, Lw_250, Lw_500, Lw_1000, Lw_2000, Lw_4000, Lw_8000 (sound power level per octave band, dB re 1 pW, unweighted). 'Create Input Layers' makes a ready-made layer.
Required. The layer must be in a projected coordinate system in metres. Selected features only are used if the layer has a selection.

param.name: out_gdb
param.dialogReference:
The file geodatabase where all results are written.
Required. Pre-filled with the default geodatabase of the project.

param.name: receivers
param.dialogReference:
The point layer with the receivers (houses, windows, measuring points). A copy is written to the geodatabase with the levels and attenuations as new fields; your layer is not changed.
Required. Projected coordinate system in metres.

param.name: rh_field
param.displayname: Receiver height field (m above ground) - empty = use the receiver height below
param.dialogReference:
Optional. Name of the field in the receiver layer with the receiver height above ground (m). A receiver with an empty value there uses the 'Receiver height' below.
Default: h_rec. If the field is empty or does not exist: all receivers use the 'Receiver height'.

param.name: barriers
param.displayname: Barriers and buildings (polygon layer with h_bar) - optional
param.dialogReference:
Optional. Polygon layer with buildings and barriers that block or reduce sound. Each polygon needs the height above ground in the field h_bar (m; field name can be changed under Advanced).
If left empty: no barriers, sound travels freely.

param.name: dem
param.displayname: Elevation raster (DEM, metres) - optional, flat ground if empty
param.dialogReference:
Optional. Elevation raster (single band, metres). It is clipped and, if needed, projected to the coordinate system of the sources. Terrain changes the heights of the sources, receivers and barriers above ground, and the ground attenuation.
If left empty: the ground is flat at 0 m.

param.name: G
param.displayname: Ground factor G (0 = hard ground, 1 = porous ground)
param.dialogReference:
Ground factor of the ground between source and receiver: 0 = hard ground (asphalt, water, concrete), 1 = porous ground (grass, soil, fields). Values between 0 and 1 are allowed.
Default: 0.5.

param.name: hr
param.displayname: Receiver height (m above ground; also for receivers without their own height)
param.dialogReference:
Height of the receiver (the 'ear') above the ground, in metres. Must be greater than 0.
Default: 1.5 m. In the map tool every cell uses it. In the receivers tool it is used for receivers that have no height of their own.

param.name: T
param.dialogReference:
Air temperature in degrees Celsius. It affects the absorption of sound by the air.
Default: 15 deg C.

param.name: RH
param.dialogReference:
Relative humidity of the air in percent (more than 0, up to 100). It affects the absorption of sound by the air.
Default: 70 %.

param.name: mode
param.dialogReference:
Which version of the ISO 9613-2 formulas the MATLAB core uses.
ISO 9613-2:2024 is the current standard. 1996 reproduces the old standard and the ISO/TR 17534-3 benchmark cases (valid for 20 deg C and 70 % humidity only). The draft amendment is experimental.
Default: ISO 9613-2:2024.

param.name: overall
param.dialogReference:
Optional. Allowed overall A-weighted level LAeq in dB(A). Cells above it are marked as failing in the pass/fail output.
If left empty: no overall limit.

param.name: band_limits
param.displayname: Allowed octave-band levels in dB, 8 values 63 ... 8000 Hz, '-' = no limit (e.g. -,-,55,50,45,40,-,-)
param.dialogReference:
Optional. Allowed levels per octave band, eight values for 63, 125, 250, 500, 1000, 2000, 4000, 8000 Hz, separated by commas. Write - for a band without limit, for example -,-,55,50,45,40,-,-. Exactly eight entries are needed.
If left empty: no band limits. A cell fails if ANY limit (overall or band) is exceeded.

param.name: weighting
param.dialogReference:
How the band limits are compared: with the unweighted band level Lp, or with the A-weighted band level LpA. Only used when band limits are given.
Default: unweighted Lp.

param.name: run_name
param.dialogReference:
Start of the name of every output of this run (for example NoiseRun_LAeq). If the name already exists in the geodatabase a number is added, so nothing is overwritten.
Default: NoiseRun (Receivers / Compare in the other tools).

param.name: add_map
param.displayname: Add the results to the active map
param.dialogReference: Add the result to the active map. Default: yes. If off, it is only written to the geodatabase.

param.name: h_field
param.dialogReference:
Name of the field in the source layer that holds the source height above ground (m).
Default: h_src.

param.name: lw_prefix
param.dialogReference:
Start of the names of the sound power fields in the source layer. The tool adds the band: with the prefix Lw_ it reads Lw_63, Lw_125 ... Lw_8000.
Default: Lw_.

param.name: b_field
param.dialogReference:
Name of the field in the barrier layer that holds the height above ground (m). Only used if a barrier layer is given.
Default: h_bar.

param.name: extra
param.displayname: Extra inputs of the MATLAB core (name=value; name=value), e.g. C0=2; groundMethod=simplified
param.dialogReference:
Optional. Extra inputs for your MATLAB core. If you added an input that the core reads from the case structure c (for example c.C0), write it here as name=value, several separated by semicolons: C0=2; groundMethod=simplified. Values can be numbers, true/false, [1 2 3] or text. Names the tool sets itself (G, mode, dem ...) are refused.
If left empty: nothing extra is passed and the core uses its own defaults.

tool.summary: Levels at receiver points: LAeq, every octave band, allowed-level check and the attenuations per band, written as new fields on a copy of the receiver layer.
